surfaces.part: full 16x16 dark teal lake-edge/grass terrain tile

answer.evidence: The candidate is a full 16x16 opaque terrain tile with a uniform dark teal texture (rows 0-15, L about 53-56 in all scanned columns). It has no silhouette, no front-edge line, no eave shadow, and no ellipse. A few lighter teal pixels at the top and left edges and one light pixel near row 13 are texture or edge details. It is a flat ground/water autotile viewed from above with no standing volume or front face, so it matches the terrain kind.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a tiny dark teal patch, far smaller than the 4x3-tile reference grass, and it reads as an almost uniform block. It has 5 raw colours and about 3 distinguishable shading steps, with only a few light pixels at the bottom as speckle. Near-flat coverage is 54%, against 0% for both references, so over half of it is flat fill. The grass reference carries tufts, clumps and several greens across every tile, and the paving reference has individually shaded stones. The candidate has no grass tufts, grain or clumps. Its visible tone count of 5 is above the grass reference's 3, but this comes from a few isolated pixels rather than real texture, so by eye it is much flatter than the references. There is no outline structure to judge, since the patch is a solid fill. As a lake-edge grass mask it does not match the reference's craft and would look like a sticker next to it.
